# Didache Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1** There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways.

**2** The way of life is this: first, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbor as yourself; and all things whatsoever you do not wish to happen to you, do not do to another.

**3** Now the teaching of these words is this: Bless those who curse you, and pray for your enemies, and fast for those who persecute you; for what credit is it if you love those who love you? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? But you — love those who hate you, and you will have no enemy.

**4** Abstain from fleshly and bodily desires. If someone strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also, and you will be perfect. If someone compels you to go one mile, go with him two. If someone takes your cloak, give him your tunic also. If someone takes from you what is yours, do not demand it back — for you are not even able to do so.

**5** Give to everyone who asks of you, and do not demand it back; for the Father wishes to give to all from his own gifts. Blessed is the one who gives according to the commandment, for he is blameless. Woe to the one who receives: if indeed someone who is in need receives, he will be blameless; but the one who does not have need will give account for why he received and for what purpose — and being put in prison, he will be examined concerning the things he did, and he will not come out from there until he has paid the last penny.

**6** But concerning this it has also been said: Let your alms sweat in your hands until you know to whom you are giving.

---

*EMET renders the Greek with maximal literalness. "Gentiles" = ἔθνη (ethnē). "Penny" = κοδράντην (kodranthēn), a Roman quadrans. "Fleshly and bodily desires" = σαρκικῶν καὶ σωματικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν.*
